summary: One shared tooltip element for every chart and the world map. Charts call `showTip()` on pointer move with HTML they have already escaped, and `hideTip()` when the pointer leaves. The tooltip is created lazily, follows the pointer and flips or clamps itself so it never leaves the window.

notes.text: File header: a single tooltip element is shared by every chart and the world map. It follows the pointer and flips sides to stay on screen.
`el` holds that one tooltip element. It starts as `null` and is only created when first needed.
`ensure()` creates the tooltip lazily, the first time any chart wants to show one.
Creates a `div` with class `tooltip`. CSS fixes it in place above everything else, makes it ignore the mouse (`pointer-events: none`) and keeps it invisible until it gets the `show` class.
`role="tooltip"` tells assistive technology what the element is.
Attaches it to the page body, only once.

The chart under the pointer can change without a `pointerleave`: closing the customer drawer with Escape removes its risk chart, a scroll moves a chart away from a still pointer, and a click can open a drawer on top. A key press, a click or a scroll anywhere therefore hides the tooltip. The listeners are added once, with the element, and `capture` also sees scrolls inside any scrolling panel.
Returns the element, whether it already existed or was just created, and closes `ensure()`.
`showTip(clientX, clientY, content)` shows the tooltip beside the pointer. The coordinates come straight from a pointer event, and `content` is HTML that the calling chart has already escaped.
Gets the shared element and replaces its content. `String()` accepts either a plain string or a `SafeHTML` object.
Adds `show`, which CSS fades in with an opacity transition.
Measures the tooltip after filling it, because its width and height depend on the content.
Horizontal position: normally 16px to the right of the pointer, but if that would run past the right edge of the window (`innerWidth`) it flips to the pointer's left side.
Vertical position: centred on the pointer, then clamped so it stays at least 8px from the top and bottom of the window.
Moves the tooltip with a CSS `transform`, which the browser can apply without recalculating the page layout, so it tracks the pointer smoothly.
Pins `left` and `top` to 0 so the translation is measured from the window's top-left corner (the element is `position: fixed`).
`hideTip()` removes `show` so the tooltip fades out. The optional chaining (`el?.`) makes it safe to call before a tooltip has ever been created.
